questions.prompt: Directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write a news report to your campus newspaper on a visit to a Hope elementary school organized by your Student Union. You should write at least 120 words but no more than 180 words.
questions.correctAnswer:
Students Bring Warmth to a Hope School

Last Sunday, our Student Union organized a visit to a Hope elementary school. Twenty students took part in the event, hoping to support local children and learn more about educational opportunities in rural areas.

The visitors brought storybooks and sports equipment collected on campus. After a brief welcome, they helped the children read simple English stories and played team games together. The children were especially interested in a science activity that explained why some objects float in water. Teachers thanked the volunteers and discussed the school's need for more reading materials.

Before leaving, the visitors promised to continue supporting the school through a regular book collection. Participants said that the experience reminded them of the importance of equal access to education. This meaningful visit connected university students with children who have different learning conditions.

questions.hint: 新闻报道应写明学生会、希望小学、具体活动和后续帮助。
questions.explanation:
以下为按题意独立写成的参考范文，作文没有唯一答案。主体按参观过程展开，结尾总结教育机会的意义；过去时保持一致。活动细节是范文设定。

结构上先交代学生会带队去希望小学，再用书籍、游戏和科学活动说明双方交流，末段写继续捐书的打算。take part in表示参加，equal access to education表示平等获得教育的机会。先后顺序可用After a brief welcome和Before leaving连接，不必每句重复then。报道体应让读者知道做了什么，再理解其意义；写“帮助儿童”时补动作和对象，避免全篇只有温暖、难忘等评价。

练习方法：先用提示列三段提纲，在30分钟内独立写作，再按下方标准逐项打分；把失分最多的一段重写。参考范文约141词（缩写、连字符词按一词，含标题或书信称呼落款），满足120–180词要求；评分用于练习自检，不代表官方阅卷分数。
rubric: 练习自评总分15分：题目覆盖0–6＋结构0–4＋语言0–5，先独立写完再对照；观点不同于范文也可得满分，只要有合理支持。
题目覆盖0–6分：该题检查——新闻报道应写明学生会、希望小学、具体活动和后续帮助。。6分=任务完整且有具体理由/活动/例证；4–5分=切题但细节偏薄；2–3分=遗漏主要任务；0–1分=基本离题。
结构0–4分：4分=开头明确任务、主体按逻辑展开、结尾回扣，段间自然；3分=顺序清楚但局部衔接生硬；1–2分=跳跃或机械罗列；0分=内容难以组织理解。
语言0–5分：5分=语法和用词基本准确、句型有变化；3–4分=少量错误但不影响理解；1–2分=反复出现时态、主谓一致或搭配错误并影响阅读；0分=多数句子不能理解。
格式与修订：按原题保持120–180词；新闻/书信/提案用对应体裁，明确要求的首句逐字保留。若超限、少写任务或缺必要格式，先修改再评分，不把字数达标当作内容满分。

questions.prompt: What does the global study tell us about people's height in the last hundred years?
questions.passage:
People have grown taller over the last century, with South Korean women shooting up by more than 20cm on average, and Iranian men gaining 16.5cm. A global study looked at the average height of 18-year-olds in 200 countries between 1914 and 2014.

The results reveal that while Swedes were the tallest people in the world in 1914, Dutch men have risen from 12th place to claim top spot with an average height of 182.5cm. Latvian women, meanwhile, rose from 28th place in 1914 to become the tallest in the world a century later, with an average height of 169.8cm.

James Bentham, a co-author of the research from Imperial College, London, says the global trend is likely to be due primarily to improvements in nutrition and healthcare. "An individual's genetics has a big influence on their height, but once you average over whole populations, genetics plays a less key role," he added.

A little extra height brings a number of advantages, says Elio Riboli of Imperial College. "Being taller is associated with longer life expectancy," he said. "This is largely due to a lower risk of dying of cardiovascular(心血管的) disease among taller people."

But while height has increased around the world, the trend in many countries of north and sub-Saharan Africa causes concern, says Riboli. While height increased in Uganda and Niger during the early 20th century, the trend has reversed in recent years, with height decreasing among 18-year-olds.

"One reason for these decreases in height is the economic situation in the 1980s," said Alexander Moradi of the University of Sussex. The nutritional and health crises that followed the policy of structural adjustment, he says, led to many children and teenagers failing to reach their full potential in terms of height.

Bentham believes the global trend of increasing height has important implications. "How tall we are now is strongly influenced by the environment we grew up in," he said. "If we give children the best possible start in life now, they will be healthier and more productive for decades to come."
